Daily Brief

The day's most significant developments center on a catastrophic glacier collapse in the Himalayas that has killed at least 360 people and left more than 1,300 missing, including hundreds of international pilgrims and tourists [BBC], [RFI], [RNZ]. Scientists say the disaster, initially mistaken for an earthquake, underscores the growing climate risks facing the rapidly warming Hindu Kush Himalaya region [BBC]. In Europe, convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladić, known as the 'Butcher of Bosnia,' died aged 84 in UN detention at The Hague, where he had been serving a life sentence for genocide at Srebrenica and the siege of Sarajevo [BBC], [France 24], [Al Jazeera]. Norway's King Harald V's health has deteriorated to 'extremely serious' condition, with the royal family gathering at his bedside and crowds laying flowers at the palace [BBC], [Le Monde]. In football governance, UEFA is preparing criminal proceedings against FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his abandoned plan to sell World Cup commercial rights to private investors for what the organization calls a 'fraudulently off-market price' [BBC], [France 24], [Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, the Pentagon is pressing NATO allies on their plans to assume greater responsibility for European defense as Washington conducts a six-month review of its force posture on the continent [The Hindu].

Top Stories
01 Climate

Himalayan Glacier Collapse Kills at Least 360, Leaves Over 1,300 Missing Including Hundreds of Tourists

  • A massive glacier collapse in Nepal near the Tibet border triggered catastrophic flooding on Wednesday, killing at least 360 people (359 in Nepal, 3 in Tibet) with more than 1,300 still missing
  • The US Geological Survey initially reported a magnitude 4.4 earthquake but later confirmed the seismic event was caused by the glacier collapse and debris flow, not tectonic activity
  • Water levels on the Trishuli River rose by up to nine meters in just 30 minutes; missing persons include at least 288 Indians, 25 Canadians, 5 New Zealanders, and pilgrims heading to sacred Mount Kailash
  • Scientists say rising temperatures are destabilizing glaciers, glacial lakes, and permafrost across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region, increasing risks of such disasters

02 Society

Ratko Mladić, 'Butcher of Bosnia' Convicted of Genocide, Dies at 84 in UN Detention

  • Ratko Mladić, the Bosnian Serb military commander convicted of genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity, died Thursday at the UN detention facility in The Hague at age 84
  • He was serving a life sentence upheld on appeal in 2021 for orchestrating the 1995 Srebrenica massacre of 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys and leading the four-year siege of Sarajevo
  • Mladić evaded capture for 16 years after the Bosnian war before being found in rural Serbia in 2011; Dutch authorities have begun an investigation into the circumstances of his death
  • The UN court's top judge ordered a full inquiry; in May, the court had rejected Mladić's bid for release despite acknowledging his 'dire' health situation

03 Society

UEFA Prepares Criminal Complaint Against FIFA President Infantino Over Failed World Cup Selloff

  • UEFA is preparing criminal proceedings in Swiss courts against FIFA President Gianni Infantino for alleged 'criminal mismanagement' over his abandoned plan to sell World Cup commercial rights
  • The plan would have created FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) to sell a 20% stake in World Cup revenues to investors including Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital for $4.2 billion
  • UEFA filed documents in US courts seeking discovery of evidence from Thrive Capital in New York and FIFA offices in Florida
  • UEFA alleges the plan was pushed through hastily with limited internal review and constituted a 'fraudulently off-market price' that would benefit Infantino's inner circle at FIFA's expense

04 Society

Norway's King Harald V in 'Extremely Serious' Condition as Royal Family Gathers

  • Norway's royal household announced that 89-year-old King Harald V's condition has become 'extremely serious' after 10 days of hospitalization for haemolytic anaemia
  • Queen Sonja, Crown Prince Haakon, and other family members cancelled engagements to gather at his bedside at Oslo University Hospital
  • Norwegians laid flowers at the palace in Oslo as the nation's public TV scrapped regular programming to cover the developing situation
  • Crown Prince Haakon, 53, has been serving as regent during his father's illness; Harald has been Europe's oldest reigning head of state since ascending the throne in 1991

Pentagon Presses NATO Allies on Plans to Assume Primary European Defense Responsibility

  • US Defence Under Secretary Elbridge Colby visited NATO headquarters in Brussels to press allies on their progress toward taking 'primary responsibility' for European conventional defense
  • Washington has sent questionnaires to European countries asking them to demonstrate how they are increasing military budgets and capabilities
  • The Trump administration launched a six-month review in July of US force deployments in Europe, raising fears among allies of potential troop reductions
  • Colby said the US aims to 'advance and accelerate' European defense responsibility while reviewing 'strategic posture' of US forces on the continent
